title: Piling up will not satisfy hunger
summary: The opening of Japji Sahib sets Truth before every age, then exposes how accumulation cannot feed the soul. Let what is forever true measure what you are trying to add.
takeaway: Let timeless Truth question the hunger for more.
lifeApplication: When the urge to add more rises, place it beside the line that Truth was here before you and will remain after you. Then decide whether the extra thing deserves your obedience.

source.shortMeaning: Truth stands before time and beyond time; piling up more cannot answer the soul's deeper hunger.
source.lifeApplication: Measure the next impulse to acquire against what remains true before, during, and after it.

evidence.coreClaim: Truth stands before time and beyond time; piling up more cannot answer the soul's deeper hunger.
evidence.turn: The shabad changes scale — the craving for more becomes small beside the Truth that precedes and outlasts every possession.
evidence.practicalImplication: When the urge to add more rises, place it beside the line that Truth was here before you and will remain after you. Then decide whether the extra thing deserves your obedience.
